terms.gloss: a stain, a spot, a mark
evidence: Paul. ex Fest. p. 121 Müll.: lābēs macula in vestīmentō dīcitur (Lewis & Short, s.v. lābēs)
terms.comment: The plain word for a spot or stain; also the spots of an animal’s coat, the mesh of a net and, by a figure, a disgrace (Lewis & Short).
The everyday verb for dirtying clothes, hands, food; also, by a figure, to corrupt.

terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica: Hor., Ov.; also post-Augustan prose
evidence: Ov. Ars 1.514: sine lābe toga (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: In Cicero only by a figure: a stain on one’s name (Lewis & Short). A different word from lābēs, a fall.
Chiefly of blood and, by a figure, of guilt (caede maculātus, Cic. Rep. 2.46); for everyday dirt, inquināre.

phrases.latin: sī inquināta erit, lavātō ā foliīs et stercore pūrgātō
phrases.english: if it is dirty, wash it and clean off the leaves and muck
Mind you don’t stain your clothes.
